turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen's gradebook said zero. Who decided that?

I have six things. One, the version history: created October 28 at 11:31 PM, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58, no earlier drafts. Two, the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in Hamlet. Three, his October 15 outline argued cowardice; the essay never mentions it. Four, on November 2 he could not tell me what epistemological paralysis means. Five, his in-class writing on September 24 was 380 words with comma splices and no quotations. Six, the checker said 94 percent.

Start with the 94 percent: that's a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says not to punish a student on it alone. I'm writing those times down. Now answer me: the zero went in before anyone called me, so who decided that?
Which of those do you want to see first?
Your case, your order. I'm still waiting on who decided the zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and an answer on who decided to enter it before anyone called me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, agreed to nothing, and still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and an answer on who entered it before calling her; that is not the fair outcome, which is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: Nothing did, because you gave her six items at once and she went straight for the weakest one, the checker score, instead of weighing the stronger ones.
What cost ground: You never owned that the zero went in before her call, and when she pressed on who decided, you asked her which item she wanted first, which handed her your job and cost you the turn.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history with its late night times on the night before the essay was due came close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open by owning in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put one dated item she can check in front of her, such as the line from Act 3 that is not in the play, and name the supervised rewrite.
